tips.title: Airbrushing Vallejo Model Air — Optimal Thinning
tips.text: Vallejo Model Air is already thin for airbrushing but can be thinned further for smoother results. Mix at a 2:1 ratio with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner (71.261). Add 2-3 drops of Vallejo Flow Improver (71.262) per 10 drops of thinned paint. Spray at 1.5-2.0 bar pressure. Test consistency on a white plastic spoon.

tips.title: Base Coating with Tamiya Spray Cans — The Two-Coat Method
tips.text: For optimal coverage, use Tamiya Spray Cans (TS-29/36) in two thin coats. Lightly sand between coats with 2000-grit wet-n-dry paper, then wipe clean with a damp cloth. Let dry for 24 hours before proceeding with detail painting.

tips.title: Camouflage Masking with Mr. Hobby Tape — The Easy Way
tips.text: Use Mr. Hobby Masking Tape (19mm) for creating clean, straight edges. Apply tape in a 'Z' or 'N' pattern to avoid edge lifting. Press firmly with a bone folder or roller. Remove tape immediately after painting each color for best results.

tips.title: Applying AK Interactive Washes — The Wipe-Off Technique
tips.text: AK Interactive Washes (AK015/025) are highly pigmented. Apply sparingly with a brush, then immediately wipe off excess with a damp cotton swab or soft cloth, working from the center outwards. Let dry, then remove residue with a clean, dry cloth.

tips.title: Chipping Technique with Sponge — Controlled Distressing
tips.text: For controlled chipping, dip a natural sea sponge (not synthetic) into a mix of Vallejo Model Color (thinned 1:1) and a touch of Vallejo Medium (71.260). Gently dab onto your model where you want chips to appear. Blot excess paint onto a paper towel before dabbing. Blow-dry between layers for faster drying.
